scenes.dialogue: Hi, I am Ravishankar from LawWorld. An F I R names Ravi. Must the police arrest him? Under the B N S S, arrest must be justified.
scenes.shown: Hi, I am Ravishankar from LawWorld. An FIR names Ravi. Must the police arrest him? Under the BNSS, arrest must be justified.

scenes.dialogue: Section Thirty Five covers arrest without a warrant. Up to seven years, the officer needs a reason to believe, and must record that necessity.
scenes.shown: Section 35 covers arrest without a warrant. Up to seven years, the officer needs a reason to believe, and must record that necessity.

scenes.dialogue: If arrest is not needed, he gets a written notice to appear. While Ravi complies, he cannot be arrested, unless fresh reasons are recorded.
Article Twenty Two and Section Forty Seven require the grounds of arrest. In Mihir Rajesh Shah, the Court held they must be written, in his own language.
scenes.shown: Article 22(1) and Section 47 require the grounds of arrest. In Mihir Rajesh Shah, the Court held they must be written, in his own language.

scenes.dialogue: Spoken grounds are for exceptional cases only. The written copy must reach him at least two hours before remand. Without it, arrest and remand are illegal.
Section Thirty Six requires an arrest memo, attested and countersigned. Section Forty Eight requires the police to inform someone he names.
scenes.shown: Section 36 requires an arrest memo, attested and countersigned. Section 48 requires the police to inform someone he names.

scenes.dialogue: Section Thirty Eight lets him meet an advocate of his choice during interrogation, though not throughout it. If the offence is bailable, he must be told.
scenes.shown: Section 38 lets him meet an advocate of his choice during interrogation, though not throughout it. If the offence is bailable, he must be told.

scenes.dialogue: Section Fifty Six protects his health. A woman is not arrested at night save exceptionally, and the infirm or over sixty need senior permission.
scenes.shown: Section 56 protects his health. A woman is not arrested at night save exceptionally, and the infirm or over 60 need senior permission.

scenes.dialogue: Section Fifty Eight caps police detention at twenty four hours, excluding necessary journey time. The Magistrate then reads the grounds and the delay. Arrest is not guilt.
scenes.shown: Section 58 caps police detention at 24 hours, excluding necessary journey time. The Magistrate then reads the grounds and the delay. Arrest is not guilt.
